To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
moral judgments are influenced by the perceived moral agency of the cognitive agents.

(1) moral judgments are different for human and non-human agents; (2) in incidental dilemmas, action is more morally permissible than the inaction; (3) for the humanoid robot the action is more appropriate and less blameworthier than for the human or automated agents.
the moral judgments of a human and an automated system are similar, but those of a humanoid robot differ from the other two.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the moral evaluation of actions and inactions is affected by the agent’s perceived moral agency.
how the moral evaluation of an agent’s action depends on the type of agent.
moral decision-making in the context of artificial cognitive agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the moral decisions of the humanoid robot are perceived to be less moral than those of the human agent, but more moral than those of a non-moral automated system.
moral agency is perceived differently for human and artificial agents.
there are no clear differences in moral judgments of human and artificial cognitive agent’s actions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the moral decisions are not necessarily the same for human and artificial agents, but the differences depend on the nature of the moral dilemma and the type of agent.

we have demonstrated the possibility of eliciting moral judgments for human and artificial agents in the same experimental paradigm and that we have found differences between the moral evaluations for the different agents.
the artificial agents are perceived as moral agents and that moral decisions are perceived differently for the human and artificial agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the moral agency of artificial cognitive agents should be considered when designing and evaluating moral behavior in artificial systems.
moral agency should not be considered a binary concept, but rather a continuum, with human and artificial agents at opposite ends.
